title: Toyota 3.5 V6 (2GR-FKS): knocking at idle from the brake vacuum pump
summary: Toyota T-SB-0115-22 Rev1: a knock at idle on Avalon, Camry, Highlander and Sienna 2GR-FKS engines that's loudest at the bank 1 head cover near the high-pressure fuel pump. After a vacuum check, the fix is a new vacuum pump, 29300-31040.

specs.name: Coolant temperature for the vacuum test
Minimum vacuum, pump dead-headed and whole system
Vacuum range where the knock should show up
Labor (USA)
specs.value: 1.8 hr Avalon and Camry; 2.4 hr 2017-2019 Highlander; 1.5 hr 2020-2022 Highlander; 1.7 hr Sienna

steps.text: Confirm a knock at idle that seems to come from the vacuum pump. If there isn't one, the bulletin doesn't apply.
Hood open, use a stethoscope. The noise should be loudest at the bank 1 head cover near the high-pressure fuel pump; if not, the bulletin doesn't apply.
Tee a vacuum gauge into the hose between the vacuum pump and the brake booster.
Engine running with coolant at 14-140 °F (-10 to 60 °C), pinch or plug the booster side. The pump must pull at least -86.7 kPa (-25.60 in Hg); if it doesn't, the bulletin doesn't apply.
Remove the pinch and read the whole system. It must also reach at least -86.7 kPa (-25.60 in Hg), which rules out a vacuum leak.

Pump the brake pedal to the floor three times to use up the vacuum, release it, and immediately watch the gauge. The bulletin applies if the knock is heard while vacuum is between -80 and -95 kPa (-23.6 to -28.05 in Hg).
Replace the vacuum pump assembly per the repair manual, then confirm the knock is reduced.

body: Tools listed: Techstream, an analog vacuum gauge and a stethoscope; a Picoscope pressure transducer kit is optional. Tacoma was removed from this bulletin in Rev1.
